transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC; Duration: 48m; Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Citrine Procurement), Derek Lowe (Citrine Legal), Samir Rao (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Security).

Summary: quick procurement/legal onboarding sync to check MSA/DPA redlines and SLA expectations before pilot.

--- Auto sections (may be imperfect) ---
Topics: MSA redline, DPA clauses, breach notification, SLAs, KMS, SSO, pricing.
Action items called out during meeting are below.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining; we know it's a busy week so we'll try to keep this tight. I'm Maya from Redwood - AE on the account.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: thanks Maya, appreciate it. quick bit of context, procurement + legal want to make sure the contract path is clear, our finance reqs and the sla so we can greenlight pilot.
[00:31] Derek Lowe: hi all, Derek here — legal. main things for us: DPA scope, subprocessor list, breach notif timing, and some questions about audit logs, where logs live.
[00:45] Jonah Ruiz: sounds good. quick intro — Jonah, solutions eng. happy to walk infra and runbook later, but on this call we can map the redlines so we know what to surface to infra.
[01:00] Samir Rao: i'm Samir, CTO. from an engineering POV we need VPC/private deployment options and KMS support, and also latency SLOs; if we push heavy traffic we need predictable p99s.
[01:18] Maya Patel: got it. on the deployment modes, Redwood has hosted, Dedicated reserve pools, and private/VPC. for pilot most customers either do hosted with VPC peering or a Dedicated reserved pool — depending on throughput and data isolation.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: clarify please: with VPC peering are keys managed by us or you? we need to know where key material resides.
[01:45] Jonah Ruiz: good call — currently we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted public API uses our KMS unless you opt for private deployment. sometimes the transcription will say "K-M-S" like kay-embess but it's KMS.
[02:06] Derek Lowe: ok. in the DPA we want explicit clause that customer controls keys and that Redwood is a processor, not a controller. also need IIAR/whatever — sorry pf, that's internal test — we want subprocessor list.
[02:26] Maya Patel: absolutely, we can provide the subprocessor list and SOC2 report. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and security pack after the call.
[02:38] Aisha Khan: pricing: finance wants a simple pilot price + an option for committed Dedicated. can you send a worksheet with both pilot and committed tier options?
[02:49] Maya Patel: yes, we'll send a pricing worksheet. for committed Dedicated we do monthly or annual commits with a baseline throughput and SLA. pilot can be a short-term eval with tokens capped.
[03:05] Derek Lowe: on SLA specifics — uptime is standard, but we also need latency SLOs for p50/p95/p99, and a remediation credit formula. do you have standard language?
[03:16] Jonah Ruiz: we have a standard SLA doc; for Dedicated we typically cover p99 tail latency targets per model family and a credit schedule. i'll include the SLA spreadsheet that maps model families to targets and credits.
[03:29] Samir Rao: important: our application is latency sensitive; p99 at 512 tokens matters. we might test with 1k seq. if the Dedicated targets don't meet, we may ask for canary or autoscale guarantees.
[03:45] Maya Patel: noted. we can propose a canary rollout and a fallback model variant if capacity impacts latency. also caching and batching configs matter — our Optimize team can recommend profiles.
[04:02] Derek Lowe: about breach notif timing: legal asked for 72 hours; your standard is 48 for incidents or is it variation?
[04:12] Jonah Ruiz: standard we aim for 48; in the DPA we can discuss resident language. sometimes procurement wants 24, which is tough. we'll need to confirm with security.
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: we will push for 72 hours max from our side — okay if you can commit to 48 but we'll see redline.
[04:35] Maya Patel: understood. i'll include the SOC2 cert and our incident response summary; that should help.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: another procurement ask — limits on liability, indemnity carveouts for data exfil, and export controls. any known friction there?
[04:56] Maya Patel: usual negotiation points, we do see liability limits around services; we can surface examples of earlier redlines. for export controls, we have a data residency and egress policy.
[05:07] Derek Lowe: DPA also needs data retention and delete procedures. if a user requests deletion, how fast does Redwood perform purge?
[05:17] Jonah Ruiz: we have retention tiers; for private deployments it's customer-controlled. for hosted we have API calls for data deletion and an internal purge workflow; timeline is typically 30 days for backups. we'll put exact language in the DPA appendix.
[05:33] Samir Rao: does Redwood offer on-prem / air-gapped option? some of our regulated workloads might require that.
[05:42] Maya Patel: yes, there's a Private deployment package for regulated workloads; it's a separate engagement and has a platform fee. we'll include a one-pager.
[05:52] Aisha Khan: thanks. procurement will want a sentencing on SLA credit calculations in the contract, so please share the spreadsheet.
[06:01] Jonah Ruiz: noted, will attach.
[06:08] Derek Lowe: question about audit logs — we need immutable audit trails, ideally streamed to our splunk or cloud logging. can Redwood stream logs or do we pull?
[06:21] Jonah Ruiz: we can push logs to customer logging endpoints for Dedicated and Private. hosted has a logs export feature but if you need real-time stream, Dedicated is best. sometimes the export gets transcribed as "log stream to splunk" but yes we support that.
[06:37] Lena Ortiz: encryption at rest and in transit — we require TLS1.2+ and AES256 at rest, plus key rotation. do you support rotation windows?
[06:47] Maya Patel: yes, we support modern TLS and AES256, key rotation is supported if customer-managed KMS.
[06:54] Aisha Khan: on the procurement timeline — what is typical time from signed MSA to pilot start if we accept the standard redlines?
[07:04] Maya Patel: usually 2-4 weeks for hosted pilot after signatures; Dedicated or Private will be longer (4-8 weeks) depending on provisioning and network.
[07:15] Samir Rao: for Dedicated we also need egress allowances and a bandwidth estimate for pricing.
[07:24] Maya Patel: we'll include bandwidth assumptions in the pricing worksheet.
[07:30] Derek Lowe: legal would like to do a single consolidated redline doc; i'll circulate our notes and ask for Redwood to respond line-by-line.
[07:38] Derek Lowe: expect that by end of week.
[07:43] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll aim to respond within 3 business days to redlines.
[07:50] Priya Nair: (interject) i'll set up the next meetings and include relevant docs in the calendar invite — security pack, SLA spreadsheet, pricing worksheet.
[08:02] Aisha Khan: great. a couple small items: are there any escrow or data escrow options?
[08:09] Maya Patel: we do have escrow options for keying in some enterprise packages; i'll flag that with our legal and include the option doc.
[08:18] Samir Rao: for the pilot we'll want a small throughput bench. can Jonah run a quick latency test with our team?
[08:26] Jonah Ruiz: yes, i'll coordinate with Samir after this call. prefer to run it in a test VPC.
[08:33] Derek Lowe: also, can you include a clear contact for security incidents and for legal escalation? usually a named SOC lead and legal contact.
[08:42] Maya Patel: yes — i'll include primary contacts and escalation matrix.
[08:47] Aisha Khan: timeline again — if we get redlines in by Friday and Redwood responds next Wed, we could do signatures the week after, goal would be end of month.
[08:59] Maya Patel: plausible. we'll try to accelerate.
[09:04] --- mid-call recap ---
[09:10] Maya Patel: recap — Redwood to send SOC2/scc? (she means SOC2), SLA spreadsheet, pricing worksheet, and KMS one-pager. Citrine legal to consolidate redlines and return by Fri. schedule technical runbook for bench tests next week.
[09:30] Derek Lowe: yes that's accurate.
[09:34] Aisha Khan: ok. a few nitty things — can we get sample SLA language for data residency (EU-only processing)?
[09:44] Jonah Ruiz: yes, we have standard clauses and regional hosting options; will include the EU-only appendix.
[09:51] Samir Rao: on the benchmarking note — we want p99 < 450ms at 512 tokens for baseline test. will that be realistic?
[10:01] Jonah Ruiz: for certain model families that's feasible on Dedicated; we'll confirm model family mapping in the SLA sheet. if not, we'll propose caching and KV tips to meet p99.
[10:14] Lena Ortiz: earlier you mentioned subprocessor list — will that be the standard list or a dynamic list?
[10:20] Maya Patel: standard list with a commitment to notify in advance of changes; we'll include a link to our subprocessor register.
[10:29] Derek Lowe: legal note: we also want right to audit clause for security compliance. is that available for enterprise packages?
[10:36] Maya Patel: right-to-audit can be accommodated for enterprise with reasonable notice — we'll add that to the redline response.
[10:45] Aisha Khan: procurement will also run a cost-benefit on pilot vs committed. please make sure pricing shows the delta and credits.
[10:55] Maya Patel: will do.
[11:00] --- Final items / closure ---
[11:05] Maya Patel: any last outstanding concerns?
[11:08] Derek Lowe: just timeline and redlines.
[11:12] Samir Rao: just the bench scheduling.
[11:15] Aisha Khan: good otherwise.
[11:18] Maya Patel: great. i'll send the docs in the next 24-48 hours. Priya will send calendar for follow-up. thanks everyone.
[11:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "KV cache" turned into "K-V cash" in earlier transcriptions; proper names may be off. References: contract redline doc (link to internal file), SLA spreadsheet (link), SOC2 summary (link).
